purpose: Test whether the D4 size-survival difference remains after both size groups are standardized to the same entry-year distribution; separately expose reporting-cadence and entry-cohort survival.
accessOrder: freeze this preregistration and its D1/D2/D4 inputs
run the fixture-only self-test and deliberate sabotage
verify all bound scripts and aggregate anchors byte-for-byte
reproduce D1 counts, D2 size groups, and D4 unstandardized survival exactly
compute the common entry-year weights before either standardized size survival
render the report only from that JSON artifact
forbiddenInputPolicy: Every other panel basename, encrypted file, or row with accepted date after 2020-12-31 aborts before aggregation.

population.entryYear: calendar year of the earliest accepted periodic filing after D1 deduplication
population.cadence: unchanged from D1: any 10-K/10-Q means quarterly; only 20-F/40-F means annual
population.identityPolicy: CIKs may exist only in process memory. No company identifier or company name may be written to an artifact or report.

commonHorizon.eligibility: a company enters the primary standardization only if the administrative cutoff is at least 12 integer calendar quarters after its entry quarter
commonHorizon.lateCohorts: later cohorts remain visible with counts and curves but never receive a carried-forward 12-quarter estimate
commonHorizon.eventCensorOrder: events are applied before censoring at the same integer duration

primaryStandardization.commonWeights: within every eligible entry year, pooled larger-plus-smaller company count divided by the total eligible larger-plus-smaller count
primaryStandardization.groupEstimate: sum over eligible years of common weight times that size group's within-year Kaplan-Meier survival at 12 quarters
primaryStandardization.statistic: standardized 12-quarter survival for smaller minus larger, in percentage points
primaryStandardization.nullModel: the two size groups have equal entry-year-standardized 12-quarter evaluability survival
primaryStandardization.threshold: absolute difference of at least 5.0 percentage points, carried forward from D2/D4 before panel access
primaryStandardization.directionCheck: the standardized and unstandardized D4 differences must have the same non-zero sign to be directionally consistent

cadenceSensitivity.statistic: annual minus quarterly Kaplan-Meier survival at 12 quarters
cadenceSensitivity.nullModel: annual-only and quarterly-reporting companies have equal 12-quarter evaluability survival
cadenceSensitivity.threshold: absolute difference of at least 5.0 percentage points is flagged descriptively

entryCohortSensitivity.statistic: maximum minus minimum 12-quarter Kaplan-Meier survival among eligible entry years with at least 200 companies
entryCohortSensitivity.nullModel: eligible entry-year cohorts have equal 12-quarter evaluability survival
entryCohortSensitivity.threshold: a range of at least 10.0 percentage points is flagged descriptively

effectiveN: unique company; the same company appears in one size group, one cadence group, and one entry cohort, so table totals are never added or treated as independent repeated observations
requiredInvariants: D1 company, event, censoring, and cadence totals reproduce exactly
D2 size company, event, and censoring totals reproduce exactly
D4 unstandardized size survival reproduces exactly
common entry-year weights sum to one and are identical for both size groups
every primary entry year contains both size groups and an estimable 12-quarter survival
all group outcomes and Kaplan-Meier curves reconcile
the output contains no company identifiers, company names, signal fields, daily observations, or post-2020 dates
explicitNonClaims: Standardization controls observed entry year only; it does not prove exchangeability or non-informative censoring.
Cadence differences partly reflect the frozen D1 event-definition cadence and are not a pure issuer effect.
The result is descriptive and not causal.
No threshold here is a study, method, or product gate.
